Surah "Al-Rahman" (Surat al-Rahman)

﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.﴾

﴿The Most Gracious﴾ ﴿taught the Qur'an﴾ ﴿created man﴾. That is: the species (al-jins), or Adam, or Muhammad (ﷺ), upon them both be peace.

﴿He taught him clear speech﴾. God, Exalted and Majestic, enumerated His blessings. He wished to mention first the one that is earliest in precedence among the kinds of His blessings and the varieties of His favours, and that is the blessing of religion (dīn). Within the blessing of religion, He mentioned what is at its highest and utmost rank, which is His bestowing the Qur'an, sending it down, and teaching it, because it is the greatest of God's revelations in rank, the highest in station, and the most beneficial in matters of religion. It is the summit of the heavenly books (kutub samāwiyya) and their confirmation, and the standard by which they are measured. He delayed the mention of the creation of man until after the mention of the Qur'an, then followed it with it, so that it would be known that He created man only for religion, and so that man might comprehensively know His revelation and His books. He placed before man that for the sake of which man was created, then mentioned what distinguishes him from the rest of the animals: al-bayān (articulate, clear expression), which is eloquent speech that clearly expresses what is in the heart. "الرَّحْمَنُ" is a mubtada' (subject of a nominal sentence). These verbs, together with their pronouns, are successive predicates (akhbār mutarādifa). Their being free of a conjunction (ʿaṭf) is because they come in the pattern of enumeration, as you would say: "Zayd enriched you after poverty, honoured you after humiliation, multiplied you after scarcity, and did to you what no one has done to anyone, so what do you deny of his kindness?!"
